name: SketchUp
tagline: Trimble's 3D modeler for quick architectural and design models, with LayOut for 2D drawings.
description: SketchUp is a 3D modeling tool from Trimble that runs on desktop, web and iPad, depending on the plan. Pro adds the desktop app and LayOut for 2D documents, and Studio adds V-Ray rendering, Scan Essentials and a Revit importer on Windows.
cons: Month-to-month Pro costs $99.99, about 3x the annual rate
freePlanDetails: SketchUp Free: browser-only modeler with 10 GB Trimble Connect storage and 3D Warehouse access. Not for commercial use.
trial: Free SketchUp Pro trial, no credit card required

plans.name: Go
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $129. Web and iPad only, no LayOut.

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $399. Desktop app and LayOut included.

plans.name: Studio
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $859. Windows only. Adds V-Ray, Scan Essentials and a Revit importer.

integrations: Trimble Connect, 3D Warehouse, V-Ray (Studio), Revit importer (Studio)

name: BricsCAD BIM
tagline: DWG-based CAD platform with a BIM toolset for building modeling and documentation.
description: BricsCAD BIM is the BIM toolset on top of BricsCAD Pro, from Bricsys, which now trades as Octave. It works natively in DWG, exchanges IFC and BCF, and is sold as a subscription or a one-time lifetime licence.
pros: Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
cons: The vendor store lists prices in euros only
Perpetual licence needs paid maintenance after year one for updates
Network licences need your own licence server
trial: 30-day free trial, no credit card required

plans.name: BIM (1-year subscription)
plans.notes: Per user. EUR 1,060 a year on the vendor store; no USD price shown. 3-year option EUR 2,860.

plans.name: BIM (lifetime licence)
plans.notes: Per user. EUR 2,376 one-time with the first year of maintenance; maintenance renewal EUR 396 a year.

plans.name: Ultimate (1-year subscription)
plans.notes: Per user. EUR 1,176 a year; bundles the BIM and Mechanical toolsets.

integrations: IFC and BCF exchange, Revit files, Unreal Engine, 3D PDF

name: Allplan
tagline: Nemetschek's BIM software for architecture, engineering and construction, sold by subscription.
bestFor: Architecture and engineering firms that model and detail in one tool
description: Allplan is BIM software from the Nemetschek Group, first released in 1984, covering 2D and 3D design through to detailing. Allplan Architecture is now sold as Allplan Concept, with Professional and Ultimate editions adding engineering and construction tools.
pros: Real-time rendering included in every edition
Wide file support including IFC, BCF, RVT, DWG, SKP and 3DM
cons: New perpetual licences ended on September 30, 2026
High price per seat compared with general CAD tools
trial: 14-day free trial (non-commercial use only), no credit card required

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: Shown 'from $140' per month on the edition comparison; billing term not stated. No building components (walls, doors, roofs).

plans.name: Concept (formerly Architecture)
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $2,892 (excl. tax).

plans.name: Professional
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $3,588 (excl. tax). Adds engineering, detailing and the Redshift renderer.

plans.name: Ultimate
plans.notes: Per user, billed yearly at $4,848 (excl. tax). Adds prefabrication and construction workflows.

integrations: IFC, BCF, RVT, DWG, DGN, SKP, 3DM; Python API; live links to Lumion and Twinmotion

name: Rhino
tagline: NURBS-based 3D modeler for freeform design, sold as a permanent licence.
description: Rhino (Rhinoceros 3D) is a 3D modeling application from Robert McNeel & Associates; Rhino 9 is the current version. It includes Grasshopper for visual scripting and Rhino Render, and is sold as a permanent licence with no maintenance fees.
pros: Permanent licence with no maintenance fees
Opens and saves DWG, DXF and SKP
cons: No built-in IFC import or export

plans.name: Upgrade
plans.notes: Per user, from an earlier Rhino version.

plans.name: Education
plans.notes: Students and faculty only, proof of status required.

integrations: Grasshopper, DWG/DXF, SKP, plug-ins such as VisualARQ for BIM and IFC

name: FreeCAD
tagline: Free, open-source parametric 3D modeler with a built-in BIM workbench.
description: FreeCAD is an open-source parametric 3D modeler released under the LGPL-2.1 licence, with no licensing fees. Since version 1.0 it has a built-in BIM workbench and reads and writes IFC.
pros: Free with no licensing fees, including commercial use
Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
cons: DWG needs a separate converter such as ODA File Converter
No vendor support, community help only
freePlanDetails: Fully free and open source (LGPL-2.1), including the BIM workbench, with no commercial-use limits.

plans.name: FreeCAD
plans.notes: Free for any number of users. Open source, LGPL-2.1.

integrations: IFC, DXF, DWG via converter, Python scripting, add-on workbenches
